security_audit.summary: Most flags reflect voxel descriptions, Markdown formatting, local asset links, or localized text. Preview rendering bypasses PowerShell execution policy and uses predictable output paths. The documentation understates preview dependencies, and the linter can echo untrusted input as report markup.

remediation.issue: Preview launches PowerShell by name with execution policy bypass.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the bypass and use a verified PowerShell executable path. Resolve and verify FFmpeg before running the compositor.

remediation.issue: Predictable render paths allow writes and manifest reads in a shared tree.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private directory for each run and confine all outputs to an approved directory. Reject links and require explicit permission to overwrite files.

remediation.issue: The local preview workflow understates dependencies and file changes.
remediation.suggestion: Document Windows PowerShell, FFmpeg, and affected output folders. Require user confirmation before starting the optional preview workflow.

remediation.issue: Prompt text is embedded directly in diagnostic Markdown.
remediation.suggestion: Use structured diagnostic output for agents and keep untrusted text in data fields. Escape text before inserting it into display Markdown.

content.value_statement: Video models can blur pixel textures or change block shapes between shots. Create consistent character references, timed storyboards, and prompts for your chosen video model.
actual_capabilities: Write character and prop cards with pixel dimensions, surface textures, and lighting choices.
Draft three-view character references and isometric prop prompts.
Build 9:16 storyboards with shot timing, camera directions, captions, and sound cues.
Format first-frame and motion prompts for Kling, Seedance, Hailuo, Wan, Sora, or Runway.
Check draft prompts for visual drift and suggest corrections for blurred textures, rounded tools, or extra fingers.
Render local voxel boards and GIF or MP4 previews on a compatible Windows setup.
limitations: Finished AI-generated clips require a separate video service. The skill does not submit prompts or images to that service.
The linter checks prompt text and reported symptoms. It does not analyze video frames.
The 30-second compiler preset repeats the original four shots. Rewrite the second half for a different sequence.
The full local preview requires Node.js, Windows PowerShell, and FFmpeg. It can overwrite generated files.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Character Reference
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Set the look for one character.
prompt_templates.prompt: Make a three-view reference prompt for an Alex-style builder holding a lantern. Specify slim arms, flat hands, sharp pixels, and warm light.

prompt_templates.title: Storyboard a Cabin Reveal
prompt_templates.scenario: Early production: Plan a vertical short.
prompt_templates.prompt: Storyboard a 15-second, 9:16 cabin reveal in four shots. Give each shot a time range, one visible action, a camera direction, and a sound cue.

prompt_templates.title: Correct Blurred Textures and Hands
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Revise a motion prompt after a test clip.
prompt_templates.prompt: My Kling clip shows blurry stone and human fingers. Rewrite the motion prompt for a miner lifting a pickaxe. Add negative terms and first-frame guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Bilingual Prompt Package
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Plan a sequence for a specific video engine.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare English and Chinese prompts for a four-shot redstone sequence in Seedance. Include first frames, motion, exclusions, camera moves, and sound cues. Keep all textures consistent.

output: Shot 1, 0 to 3.8 seconds: Alex places a crafting table on grass. Use a fixed isometric view and a wooden placement cue.
Shot 2, 3.8 to 7.5 seconds: Alex places a hinged chest beside the table. Use a close view and a soft click.
Shot 3, 7.5 to 11.3 seconds: Alex hangs the lantern. Keep the camera still as warm light reaches the cabin walls.
Shot 4, 11.3 to 15 seconds: Alex sits beside the cabin. Pull back slowly and let the placement sounds fade.

output_examples.input: Fix a mining prompt that produces human fingers and soft textures.
output_examples.output: Start from a still with fingerless square hands and crisp 16x16 stone textures. Animate one rigid shoulder swing. Exclude human fingers, smooth handles, and blurred pixels.

best_practices: Reuse the same character and prop references across shots to keep scale, outfit, and textures consistent.
Give each shot one primary action and at most one camera move.
Choose the target video model before writing motion prompts and inspect a first frame before animating.
anti_patterns: Describe the subject only as a blocky toy without specifying shape or pixel size.
Combine several character actions and rapid camera changes in one short clip.
Treat a local preview as the final video from your chosen AI model.

faq.question: Does this skill generate the finished video?
faq.answer: It provides prompts, boards, and optional local previews. Use a separate video model for the final generated clips.

faq.question: Which video models have prompt formats?
faq.answer: The skill provides formats for Kling, Seedance or Jimeng, Hailuo, Wan, Sora, and Runway.

faq.question: What is a first-frame reference?
faq.answer: It is a still image that defines the character, props, lighting, and framing before you generate motion.

faq.question: Can I get prompts in English and Chinese?
faq.answer: Yes. Request bilingual output for character references, motion prompts, or prompt corrections.

faq.question: Can the linter inspect a finished clip?
faq.answer: No. Provide the draft prompt or describe a visible defect to get a suggested rewrite.

faq.question: What is required for local GIF and MP4 previews?
faq.answer: The bundled preview workflow needs Node.js, Windows PowerShell, and FFmpeg. It writes generated assets into skill folders.
